Title: Ovulation Pain: More Than 40% Of Women Get It, And For Many It's Almost Every Month

Description:
Ever get a sharp twinge on one side of your lower belly right in the middle of your cycle? That's ovulation pain — it affects more than 40% of women of reproductive age, and for many it happens almost every month.

A growing follicle stretches the ovary's surface, then fluid released when it ruptures irritates your abdominal lining. Prostaglandins drive both steps, which is why heat and an NSAID like ibuprofen at the first sign of pain both work well.

Tracking your cycle helps too — mark the days you expect ovulation so you're not caught off guard.

See a doctor if the pain lasts more than 48 hours, or comes with nausea, vomiting, or dizziness — sudden severe one-sided pain needs urgent care.
